title: Trading Policy

tiers.name: Staff
tiers.description: Permanent Insiders, full-time, part-time and casual employees, and contractors, consultants and advisers of the Company and its Related Bodies Corporate. Subject to the general insider trading prohibition, the 6-month short-term/speculative trading ban, and the extension of the insider trading prohibition to dealings through Associates.

tiers.name: Permanent Insiders
tiers.description: Persons having authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the Company's activities, including directors and key executives, and other individuals placed on the Company's permanent insiders list maintained on the EQS platform (for German capital markets law compliance). Subject to Closed Periods, prior written approval before dealing, and notification of the Company Secretary within 2 business days.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of the Company, a subset of Permanent Insiders, additionally subject to ASX Listing Rule notification of changes in relevant interests and, under German law, BaFin substantial-shareholding threshold notification.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Nominees, agents or other associates of Staff, such as family members, family trusts and family companies, through whom dealings are also caught by the insider trading prohibition.

windows.start_anchor: 30 calendar days prior to release of the Company's Annual Report or relevant announcement
windows.end_anchor: 48 hours after release of the Company's Annual Report or relevant announcement

windows.start_anchor: 30 calendar days prior to release of the consolidated interim of the Company or relevant announcement
windows.end_anchor: 48 hours after release of the consolidated interim of the Company or relevant announcement

windows.start_anchor: 30 calendar days prior to release of the Company's quarterly reports or relevant announcement (if applicable)
windows.end_anchor: 48 hours after release of the Company's quarterly reports or relevant announcement (if applicable)

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may at its discretion vary a Closed Period by general announcement to Permanent Insiders, before or during the Closed Period (not stated as confidential). Separately, any Permanent Insider in possession of price sensitive information not generally available to the market must not deal at any time, regardless of Closed Periods.

rules.detail: Securities is defined narrowly as ordinary shares and other securities of the Company on issue; the policy does not mention derivatives, options written by third parties, or any financial product created over or referencing Company Securities. An OTC put or call with a bank is not named or otherwise swept into the Dealing/approval regime.
No hedging provision, definition of hedging, or reference to limiting economic risk appears anywhere in the policy.

Prepaid forwards, collars or other monetisation structures are not named and are not caught by the narrow Securities/Dealing definitions, which are limited to buying, selling or procuring another to buy or sell Company shares/securities.
Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
CFDs are not mentioned and are not caught by the narrow Securities/Dealing definitions.

Margin lending using Company Securities as collateral is contemplated and not prohibited. If the lender exercises its rights on default, the resulting disposal is listed as an exception Staff may make at any time (including during a Closed Period) and is expressly stated not to breach insider trading laws.
rules.evidence: dispose of Securities of the Company resulting from a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement;

rules.detail: Providing Company Securities to a lender as security by mortgage or charge is expressly contemplated. Only the resulting default sale is addressed; the initial grant of security is not itself treated as a 'Dealing' requiring approval or notification.
rules.evidence: Where Company Securities are provided to a lender as security by way of mortgage or charge, a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.

rules.detail: Secured financing generally (mortgage, charge or margin lending) over Company Securities is not prohibited for any tier. A lender's forced sale on default is expressly excused from both the Closed Period restriction and the general insider trading prohibition, with no requirement for prior clearance of that sale.
rules.evidence: Where Company Securities are provided to a lender as security by way of mortgage or charge, a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.

rules.detail: Short-term or speculative trading, defined as holding Company shares for less than 6 months, is banned for all Staff, with a carve-out for exercising convertible securities where the shares are sold shortly after exercise.
rules.evidence: It is prohibited for any member of Staff to engage in short-term trading of the Company's Securities except, subject to the other terms of these guidelines for the exercise of convertible Securities where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter.

clearance.approver: Managing Director (Chairman of the Board if the Permanent Insider dealing is the Managing Director; all other Board members if the Permanent Insider dealing is the Chairman)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 2 business days of the transaction occurring
clearance.evidence: Any member of the Permanent Insiders (other than the Chairman of the Board or the Managing Director) wishing to buy, sell or exercise rights in relation to the Company's Securities must obtain the prior written approval of the Managing Director before doing so.

short_term.basis: shares held for less than 6 months
carve_outs: exercise of convertible Securities where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter
short_term.evidence: In this document, short-term or speculative trading refers to trading in Company where the shares are held for less than 6 months.

exceptions.approver: Managing Director (or Chairman of the Board or all other Board members, as applicable)
exceptions.evidence: Permanent Insiders who are not in possession of inside information ... may be given prior written clearance ... to sell or otherwise dispose of Company Securities in a Closed Period where the person is in severe financial hardship.

exceptions.approver: Managing Director (or Chairman of the Board or all other Board members, as applicable)
exceptions.evidence: Exceptional circumstances may apply to the disposal of Company Securities by a Permanent Insider if the person is required by a court order or a court enforceable undertaking ... to transfer or sell Securities of the Company.
acquire, or agree to acquire or exercise (but not sell Securities following exercise) convertible Securities under an employee incentive scheme (as that term is defined in the ASX Listing Rules);
trade under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided in accordance with procedures set out in this Policy.
dispose of Securities of the Company resulting from a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement;
undertake to accept, or accept, a takeover offer;
acquire Company Securities under a dividend reinvestment, or top-up plan that is available to all holders or Securities of the same class;

trade under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back.

exemption_authority: Managing Director (or Chairman of the Board if the Managing Director is dealing, or all other Board members if the Chairman is dealing) may grant a written exemption from Closed Period restrictions for severe financial hardship or exceptional circumstances (court order, overriding legal/regulatory requirement), only if the person is not in possession of inside information; the exemption specifies a time period for the sale. Not stated to be confidential.
jurisdiction_overlays: Germany: BaFin notification under Section 33 of the German Securities Trading Act; EU Market Abuse Regulation No. 596/2014 (MAR)

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where Company Securities are provided to a lender as security by way of mortgage or charge, a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares on default is expressly excused from both the insider trading prohibition and the Closed Period restriction, which materially de-risks the lender's security position under a funded collar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Securities is defined as ordinary shares and other securities in the Company; the policy contains no hedging clause and does not name derivatives or third-party financial products anywhere.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An OTC put and call with a bank over Company shares falls outside the policy's Dealing, Closed Period and approval mechanics entirely, so the derivative legs of the collar are not independently restricted (though general insider trading law still applies).

bespoke_clauses.clause: the management of the sale of any significant volume of Company Securities (i.e. a volume that would represent a volume in excess of 10% of the total Securities held by the seller prior to the sale, or a volume to be sold that would be in excess of 10% of the average daily traded volume ... for the preceding 20 trading days) by Staff needs to be discussed with the Board and the Company's legal advisers prior to the execution of any sale.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unwinding or physically settling a large collar position could trigger this pre-execution Board/legal-adviser discussion requirement, adding a further approval step beyond ordinary clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: short-term or speculative trading refers to trading in Company where the shares are held for less than 6 months.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar structured to unwind or be exercised within 6 months of the shares being acquired could be characterised as prohibited short-term trading.

summary: A funded collar appears structurally available under this policy. 'Securities' is defined narrowly as Company-issued shares and securities, so an OTC put and call with a bank are not named or caught by any dealing, closed-period or approval mechanic, and the policy separately contemplates providing Company Securities to a lender as security by mortgage or charge, with a lender's forced sale on default expressly excused from both the Closed Period restriction and insider trading liability. A Permanent Insider (director or key executive) must still obtain prior written approval from the Managing Director (escalating to the Chairman or Board), execute outside the 30-day-before/48-hour-after Closed Periods around annual, interim and quarterly results (or under a written hardship/exceptional-circumstances exemption), and notify the Company Secretary within 2 business days. Entry and unwind must also respect the 6-month minimum holding period against short-term or speculative trading. Any sale exceeding 10% of the individual's holding or of 20-day average volume, such as unwinding the collar, requires prior discussion with the Board and the Company's legal advisers. Because the policy is silent on derivatives and hedging generally, the funded collar is not expressly regulated as such, and compliance turns mainly on the clearance, timing and volume conditions described above rather than an outright prohibition.
